label: UniFi U6 Extender
description: A plug-in WiFi 6 mesh extender: no Ethernet port at all, one radio pair (4x4 5 GHz, 2x2 2.4 GHz) and a wall plug. It only reaches the network through a mesh uplink, which is the reason to model it with radios and no copper.
notes: Vendor figures: no networking interface listed - the U6 Extender is a wall-plug mesh unit with no Ethernet port; max data rate 4.8 Gbps on 5 GHz (4x4, BW160) and 573.5 Mbps on 2.4 GHz (2x2, BW40); universal AC input 100-240V. Mesh uplink only: in a lab it can join a wireless mesh but cannot be cabled, which is a real constraint of the hardware.

label: UniFi U7 Pro XG
description: WiFi 7 access point with a single 10GbE port and PoE++ - the 10G uplink is the point, so an AP is no longer the bottleneck on a 10G access switch.
notes: Vendor figures: (1) 10 GbE RJ45 port; max data rate 5.8 Gbps on 6 GHz (2x2), 4.3 Gbps on 5 GHz (2x2), 688 Mbps on 2.4 GHz (2x2); power method PoE++. Modelled with a 25.5 W PoE input (802.3at/PoE++ floor) because the vendor lists PoE++ without a wattage figure.

label: UniFi U7 Pro XGS
description: The 4x4 5 GHz variant of the U7 Pro XG: same single 10GbE PoE++ port, but 8.6 Gbps on 5 GHz instead of 4.3 - twice the spatial streams where most clients actually are.
notes: Vendor figures: (1) 10 GbE RJ45 port; max data rate 5.8 Gbps on 6 GHz (2x2), 8.6 Gbps on 5 GHz (4x4), 688 Mbps on 2.4 GHz (2x2); PoE++. The 4x4 5 GHz radio is what separates it from U7-Pro-XG.

label: UniFi AC HD
description: WiFi 5 access point with two GbE ports, 4x4 on both bands and 1.7 Gbps on 5 GHz. One port daisy-chains a second AP, which is why it carries two.
notes: Vendor figures: (2) GbE RJ45 ports; max data rate 1.7 Gbps on 5 GHz (4x4 MU-MIMO) and 800 Mbps on 2.4 GHz (4x4); power method PoE+. The second GbE port is a passthrough for daisy-chaining, so both are modelled as ordinary ports.

label: UniFi AC SHD
description: The shielded-radio AC access point: two GbE ports, 4x4 on both bands, plus a dedicated security radio for wireless intrusion detection.
notes: Vendor figures: (2) GbE RJ45 ports; max data rate 1.7 Gbps on 5 GHz and 800 Mbps on 2.4 GHz, both 4x4 MU-MIMO; power method PoE+. The third (security) radio is not modelled as a forwarding interface - it is a monitoring radio, not a data path.

label: UniFi FlexHD
description: A compact indoor/outdoor AC access point: one GbE port, 4x4 on 5 GHz and 2x2 on 2.4 GHz, mountable on a wall, ceiling or pole.
notes: Vendor figures: (1) GbE RJ45 port; max data rate 1.7 Gbps on 5 GHz (4x4 MU-MIMO) and 300 Mbps on 2.4 GHz (2x2); power method PoE.

label: UniFi XG
description: The 10G access point: one GbE port and one 1/10 GbE ICM port, 4x4 on 5 GHz at 1733 Mbps. Needs a PoE++ injector - it will not run from 802.3af.
notes: Vendor figures: (1) GbE RJ45 port and (1) 1/10 GbE ICM Ethernet port; max data rate 1733 Mbps on 5 GHz (4x4) and 450 Mbps on 2.4 GHz (3x3); power method: Gigabit PoE++ adapter 50V DC 1.2A. The second port is the 10G ICM interface, modelled at 10G.

label: UniFi nanoHD
description: A small AC Wave 2 access point: one GbE port, 4x4 on 5 GHz and 2x2 on 2.4 GHz, designed to be unobtrusive on a ceiling.
notes: Vendor figures: (1) GbE RJ45 port; max data rate 1.7 Gbps on 5 GHz (4x4 MU-MIMO) and 300 Mbps on 2.4 GHz (2x2); power method PoE.
